# Mobile Terminal for Multimedia File Processing

The mobile terminal comprises several interconnected units that work together to process and modify multimedia content, as described below.

## Decoding Unit

The mobile terminal includes a decoding unit configured to obtain and decode a first multimedia file. Through this decoding process, the unit produces multiple frames of decoded first pictures, along with a corresponding time parameter. This time parameter preserves the temporal relationship between the individual frames, ensuring that the sequence and timing of the original content are retained for subsequent processing.

## First Processing Unit

A first processing unit is responsible for capturing a first input operation. This operation is applied to any selected frame among the decoded first pictures. By detecting and receiving this user input, the first processing unit identifies a specific first area within the selected frame, thereby establishing the region of interest that will guide the subsequent processing steps.

## Second Processing Unit

The second processing unit performs two key functions:

**Area Identification.** First, the second processing unit identifies the area in every other frame that corresponds to the first area of the selected frame. Each of these corresponding regions is designated as the first area of its respective frame. In this way, the region of interest originally defined in the selected frame is consistently mapped across all frames of the decoded first pictures.

**Predetermined Processing.** Next, the second processing unit performs predetermined processing on the areas outside the first areas across all frames. By applying this processing to the regions surrounding the designated first areas, the unit generates multiple frames of second pictures, which reflect the modifications made to the content outside the areas of interest.

## Encoding Unit

Finally, an encoding unit encodes the multiple frames of second pictures according to the time parameter. By utilizing the previously preserved timing information, the encoding unit reassembles the processed frames in their correct temporal sequence to generate a second multimedia file. This resulting file represents the fully processed output, incorporating all modifications while maintaining the original timing characteristics of the content.

# Information Processing Method, Mobile Terminal, and Computer Storage Medium

## Technical Field

The present disclosure relates to the field of information processing technology, and more particularly, to an information processing method, a mobile terminal, and a computer storage medium for automated region-based editing of multimedia files.

## Background

With the widespread adoption of mobile terminals equipped with high-resolution cameras, users increasingly capture and share video content in their daily lives. However, editing video content—particularly performing consistent modifications to a specific region across an entire video sequence—remains a technically challenging and labor-intensive task. Conventional editing methods typically require a user to manually identify and adjust the target region within each individual frame of a video. Because a single video may contain hundreds or thousands of frames, such frame-by-frame manual editing is time-consuming, prone to inconsistency, and impractical for the average user operating a mobile device. There exists a need for an efficient method that allows a user to designate a region of interest a single time and have the corresponding editing operation propagated automatically and consistently throughout the entire video.

## Summary of the Disclosure

To address the foregoing limitations, this disclosure presents an information processing method, a mobile terminal, and a computer storage medium that enable automated region-based editing across an entire video sequence based on a single frame selection.

In general terms, the method operates as follows. A first multimedia file—such as a video file—is obtained and decoded into a plurality of individual frames. A user input operation is received with respect to one of these frames, whereby the user selects an area, or region of interest, within that particular frame. Based on the selected area in the single frame, the system identifies the corresponding areas across all other frames of the multimedia file. The system then processes the non-selected areas—that is, the portions of each frame lying outside the identified region of interest—so as to generate a plurality of new, processed frames. Finally, the system re-encodes these processed frames in accordance with the time parameter of the original multimedia file, thereby producing a second multimedia file that reflects the desired editing operation applied consistently throughout the sequence.

## Detailed Description

### Decoding the Multimedia File

In an initial step, the mobile terminal acquires a first multimedia file. This file may be captured directly by an image acquisition component of the terminal, retrieved from local storage, or received from an external source such as a network server. The multimedia file is then decoded into a plurality of frames, each frame representing a still image corresponding to a specific moment in the playback timeline. During decoding, the system also extracts a time parameter associated with the multimedia file, which may include frame rate, timestamp, and sequence information necessary to reconstruct the file after processing.

### Receiving the User Selection

After decoding, at least one frame is presented to the user through a display interface of the mobile terminal. The user performs an input operation—for example, a touch gesture, a drawing motion, or a boundary-tracing action—to select an area within the displayed frame. This selected area defines the region of interest that the user wishes to preserve or otherwise treat differently from the remainder of the image. The selection may correspond to a foreground object, a subject of interest, or any arbitrary shape designated by the user.

### Identifying Corresponding Areas Across Frames

Once the area has been selected in the single reference frame, the system automatically identifies the areas in all other frames that correspond to the selected region. This identification may be accomplished using techniques such as feature matching, object tracking, edge detection, motion estimation, or similar image analysis methods. By tracking the selected region through the sequence, the system accounts for movement, deformation, and changes in position of the region of interest as it appears across successive frames. In this way, a single user selection is intelligently propagated throughout the entire video sequence without requiring further manual input.

### Processing the Non-Selected Areas

Having identified the region of interest in each frame, the system processes the non-selected areas—the portions of each frame outside the region of interest—to generate a plurality of new frames. The processing applied to the non-selected areas may take various forms depending on the desired editing effect. For example, the non-selected areas may be blurred, darkened, desaturated, converted to grayscale, replaced with a solid color or alternative background, or otherwise visually modified. As a result, the region of interest is highlighted or isolated relative to its surroundings in a consistent manner across every frame of the sequence.

### Re-Encoding into a Second Multimedia File

Finally, the plurality of processed frames is re-encoded to produce a second multimedia file. The re-encoding is performed in accordance with the time parameter extracted from the original multimedia file, ensuring that the processed frames are reassembled in the correct order and at the appropriate playback rate. Consequently, the second multimedia file preserves the temporal characteristics of the original while reflecting the region-based editing operation throughout its entirety.

## Mobile Terminal

The disclosure further provides a mobile terminal configured to perform the above method. The mobile terminal may include a processor, a memory, a display, and an input component. The processor is configured to decode the first multimedia file into a plurality of frames, receive a user input operation selecting an area in one frame, identify corresponding areas across the other frames, process the non-selected areas to generate new frames, and re-encode the processed frames according to the time parameter to produce the second multimedia file.

## Computer Storage Medium

The disclosure additionally provides a computer storage medium storing computer-executable instructions. When executed by a processor, the instructions cause the processor to carry out the steps of the information processing method described above, including decoding, region selection, cross-frame region identification, non-selected-area processing, and re-encoding.

## Technical Advantages

By enabling a user to make a single region selection and automatically propagating the corresponding editing operation across all frames of a video, the present disclosure significantly reduces the time and effort required for region-based video editing. The method eliminates the need for tedious frame-by-frame manual adjustment, improves the consistency of the resulting edits, and makes advanced editing capabilities accessible to ordinary users operating mobile terminals with limited input capabilities.

# The Embodiments

The concept of embodiment sits at the crossroads of philosophy, cognitive science, and everyday human experience. To speak of embodiments is to acknowledge that ideas, forms, and possibilities do not exist in a vacuum—they take shape, they assume physical presence, and they become tangible through the bodies and objects that carry them into the world.

## The Meaning of Embodiment

At its core, an embodiment is the particular form that an abstract idea or principle takes when it becomes concrete. A single concept can have many embodiments. Consider the idea of "shelter": it may be embodied in a tent, a house, a cave, or a skyscraper. Each is a distinct realization of the same underlying purpose, yet none exhausts the full range of what the concept could become. In this sense, the embodiments of an idea are windows into its flexibility and its enduring relevance.

## Embodiment in Human Experience

Philosophers such as Maurice Merleau-Ponty argued that the body is not merely a vessel we inhabit but the very foundation of how we perceive and understand the world. We think through our bodies, we know through our senses, and we relate to others through gesture, expression, and presence. From this perspective, human beings are themselves embodiments—of memory, of culture, of history, and of possibility. Our understanding is never purely intellectual; it is grounded in the flesh, in movement, and in the lived encounter with our surroundings.

## Embodiments in Design and Invention

In more practical domains, the term "embodiments" appears frequently in patents and technical descriptions, where it refers to the specific ways an invention can be constructed or applied. A single innovation might be described through several embodiments, each illustrating a different configuration or use. This language reflects a deep truth about creativity: a good idea is rarely limited to one manifestation. Its value lies in its capacity to be reimagined, adapted, and re-expressed across many contexts.

## Conclusion

The embodiments of any concept—whether philosophical, artistic, or technical—remind us that meaning becomes real only when it takes form. To study embodiments is to appreciate the bridge between thought and matter, between what is imagined and what is made. In every embodiment, we witness the ongoing dialogue between the abstract and the concrete, a dialogue that shapes both the objects we create and the lives we lead.

# Abstract

A method and mobile terminal for processing multimedia files are disclosed. The method comprises decoding a multimedia file to obtain a plurality of video frames, and displaying at least one of the decoded frames on a display of the mobile terminal. In response to a user input, a target area is selected within a displayed frame. The mobile terminal identifies corresponding areas in one or more other frames of the plurality of video frames based on the selected target area. A predetermined processing operation is then applied to the selected target area and to the identified corresponding areas across the plurality of frames. The processed frames are subsequently re-encoded to generate a processed multimedia file. The processing operation may include one or more of blurring, mosaicking, occluding, brightening, color adjustment, or replacement of image content within the selected and corresponding areas. By enabling region-specific processing to be propagated automatically across multiple frames, the method allows a user to efficiently edit or modify localized portions of a video directly on a mobile terminal without requiring frame-by-frame manual editing, thereby improving processing efficiency and user convenience.

# SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The following presents a simplified summary of the present invention in order to provide a basic understanding of some aspects of the disclosure. This summary is not an extensive overview and is not intended to identify key or critical elements or to delineate the scope of the invention.

## Overview

The present invention relates generally to video editing systems and methods, and more particularly to systems and methods for applying visual effects across multiple frames of a video on a mobile computing device based on a user selection made within a single frame.

## Problem Addressed

Conventional video editing on mobile devices typically requires a user to manually apply an effect to individual frames or to define effect boundaries repeatedly across a video timeline. Such approaches are time-consuming, computationally inefficient, and often produce inconsistent results, particularly where a selected region moves, changes shape, or changes position across successive frames. These limitations are compounded on mobile devices, which have constrained processing resources, limited display area, and touch-based input mechanisms that make precise, repeated selections difficult.

## Summary of the Solution

In one aspect, the present invention provides a method for editing video on a mobile device, the method comprising:

- **receiving**, via a touch interface of the mobile device, a user input designating a region of interest within a single selected frame of a video comprising a plurality of frames;

- **receiving** a selection of a visual effect to be applied to the designated region;

- **identifying**, using an object-tracking or feature-tracking process, corresponding regions in one or more additional frames of the video that correspond to the designated region in the selected frame; and

- **automatically applying** the selected visual effect to the corresponding regions across the plurality of frames without requiring additional user selection input for each frame.

In certain embodiments, the corresponding regions are identified by tracking one or more visual features, edges, color characteristics, or motion vectors associated with the designated region across successive frames, such that the applied effect follows the region as it changes in position, size, orientation, or shape throughout the video.

In further embodiments, the visual effect includes one or more of a blur, color adjustment, brightness or contrast modification, pixelation, overlay, masking, stylization, or object removal effect applied selectively to the tracked region.

In another aspect, the invention provides a mobile computing device comprising a processor, a touch-sensitive display, and a memory storing instructions that, when executed by the processor, cause the device to perform the operations described above.

In a further aspect, the invention provides a non-transitory computer-readable medium storing instructions that, when executed by one or more processors of a mobile device, cause the mobile device to perform the described method.

## Advantages

Among other advantages, embodiments of the present invention enable a user to apply an effect consistently across an entire video sequence through a single-frame selection, thereby reducing the number of user interactions, decreasing editing time, and improving consistency of the applied effect. Certain embodiments further optimize processing for resource-constrained mobile hardware, enabling real-time or near-real-time preview and application of effects.

The foregoing summary is illustrative only and is not intended to be limiting. Additional aspects, features, and advantages of the invention will become apparent from the detailed description, drawings, and claims that follow.

---

# Summary of the Invention

The present invention provides an information processing method, a mobile terminal, and a computer storage medium that address the aforementioned limitations of the prior art by enabling efficient frame-by-frame decoding in combination with area-based image processing to improve processing accuracy and reduce computational overhead.

According to a first aspect of the present invention, there is provided an information processing method, the method comprising: acquiring a target video stream to be processed, wherein the target video stream comprises a plurality of image frames; decoding the target video stream on a frame-by-frame basis to obtain a plurality of decoded image frames; determining, for at least one of the decoded image frames, one or more target processing areas within the image frame according to a predetermined image characteristic; performing an image processing operation on the one or more target processing areas to generate processed image data; and outputting a processing result based on the processed image data.

In one possible implementation, the step of determining the one or more target processing areas comprises identifying a region of interest within the decoded image frame based on at least one of pixel value distribution, feature point detection, or object recognition, and defining the region of interest as the target processing area, whereby image processing is selectively applied to the target processing area rather than to the entire image frame, thereby reducing the amount of data to be processed.

In a further possible implementation, the frame-by-frame decoding and the area-based image processing are performed in a pipelined manner, such that a subsequent image frame is decoded while a current image frame is subjected to the image processing operation, thereby improving overall processing efficiency and reducing latency.

According to a second aspect of the present invention, there is provided a mobile terminal, comprising a processor and a memory configured to store a computer program executable on the processor, wherein the processor, when executing the computer program, is configured to implement the steps of the information processing method described above.

According to a third aspect of the present invention, there is provided a computer storage medium having a computer program stored thereon, wherein the computer program, when executed by a processor, implements the steps of the information processing method described above.

By virtue of the above technical solutions, the present invention achieves at least the following advantageous effects: the frame-by-frame decoding ensures that each image frame is accurately and independently processed, while the area-based image processing concentrates computational resources on the target processing areas, thereby enhancing processing precision, reducing power consumption and memory usage, and improving the responsiveness of the mobile terminal.

# Functional Units of a Mobile Terminal for Video Frame Modification

## Technical Description in Patent Language

The following describes the functional units of a mobile terminal configured for modifying selected areas across a plurality of video frames.

---

### Decoding Unit

A decoding unit is configured to receive an encoded video stream and decode said encoded video stream into a plurality of successive video frames, wherein each of said plurality of video frames comprises image data representable in a decoded format suitable for subsequent processing, said decoding unit being further operable to output said plurality of decoded video frames to at least the first processing unit.

---

### First Processing Unit

A first processing unit is communicatively coupled to said decoding unit and configured to receive said plurality of decoded video frames, said first processing unit being operable to:

- **identify** at least one selected area within at least one of said plurality of video frames, wherein said selected area corresponds to a designated region of interest;
- **determine** spatial coordinates and boundary parameters defining said selected area; and
- **generate** region identification data corresponding to said selected area,

wherein said first processing unit is further configured to transmit said region identification data and said associated video frames to the second processing unit.

---

### Second Processing Unit

A second processing unit is communicatively coupled to said first processing unit and configured to receive said region identification data and said associated video frames, said second processing unit being operable to:

- **apply** at least one modification operation to said selected area in accordance with said region identification data, said modification operation comprising one or more of a visual alteration, a substitution, an obscuration, or an enhancement of image data within said selected area;
- **propagate** said modification operation across a subset of said plurality of video frames such that said selected area is consistently modified throughout said subset; and
- **produce** a plurality of modified video frames,

wherein said second processing unit outputs said plurality of modified video frames to the encoding unit.

---

### Encoding Unit

An encoding unit is communicatively coupled to said second processing unit and configured to receive said plurality of modified video frames, said encoding unit being operable to encode said plurality of modified video frames into an encoded output video stream in a predetermined format, and to output said encoded output video stream for at least one of storage, transmission, or display.

---

## Notes on Usage

- **Means-plus-function alternative:** Each unit may alternatively be claimed using "means for" language (e.g., "means for decoding an encoded video stream") if invoking 35 U.S.C. § 112(f) is intended.
- **Structural correspondence:** For enablement, the specification should link each functional unit to corresponding structure (e.g., processor, memory, dedicated hardware, or software modules).
- **Flexibility:** Terms such as "communicatively coupled" and "operable to" preserve claim breadth while maintaining functional definiteness.

# Patent Abstract

## Method and System for Region-Based Multimedia Processing with Selective Background Modification

**Abstract:**

A system and method for processing multimedia content is disclosed, comprising decoding a first multimedia file into a plurality of constituent frames. The method includes receiving user input designating at least one region of interest within one or more of the decoded frames. Based on the user input, a corresponding region is identified and tracked across a sequence of the plurality of frames, wherein the region identification is propagated temporally to maintain spatial correspondence of the designated region throughout successive frames. The system distinguishes between the identified region and one or more background areas within each frame, wherein the background areas comprise portions of the frame outside the identified region. At least one processing operation is applied to the background areas while substantially preserving the identified region, the processing operation including one or more of blurring, color modification, replacement, occlusion, or resolution adjustment. The processed frames, comprising the preserved identified region and the modified background areas, are subsequently encoded to generate a second multimedia file. In certain embodiments, the region tracking employs motion estimation between adjacent frames to reduce user input requirements across the frame sequence. The invention enables efficient, targeted modification of multimedia content while maintaining visual integrity of user-selected regions, with applications in privacy protection, content editing, and selective visual enhancement.
